title: Pell Glassworks
youtube_title: He drove her to a shut glassworks. She learned glass there
logline: To prove the signature isn't hers, Nora needs a place to work. Elias drives her to Pell Glassworks — where she interned at nineteen, shut for twelve years.
hook: Dawn. Elias parks at the end of a grey street. "You want to prove it. You need a place." Over the steel door, faded letters: PELL GLASSWORKS.
mid_hook: She gets out and stops. Flashback: nineteen, ponytail, this same door. A young man in rimless glasses smiles and holds out a card. "Grant Whitlock. Sales manager."
extra_hooks: Next door, a small shopfront under dust: CLAIRE QUINN GLASS — her mother's closed studio. The padlock has rusted shut. She touches it. No key. She doesn't push.
conflict: Dana filed a forgery complaint with the prosecutor's office this morning, but the proof is on Nora. She needs a furnace and a place to make samples — and Elias has brought her to the one place she never wanted to see again.
turn: She thought he was renting her an empty warehouse. Then the car stops, and it's Pell's — where she learned to blow glass, and where she met Grant. "How do you own this place?" "Bought it at auction."

cliffhanger.text: Elias takes a call and walks back to the car. "I'll wait here." Alone, she shoves the steel door. Twelve years of dust rolls out. Deep inside, a huge furnace under a tarp. A flashlight hits her face. A rough voice: "Who's there?"
cliffhanger.question: Who's holding the flashlight?

spectacle: A whole row of dead glassworks on Kiln Row, steel doors rusted dark red; morning light slants through broken high windows into a sheet of hanging dust.
glamour_shot: Nora at the PELL GLASSWORKS door, shoulder-length hair lifted by the wind off the water, looking up at the faded letters with twelve-year-old light in her eyes.
general_payoffs: She has a possible studio: Pell's on Kiln Row
She learns Elias bought Pell's at auction

title: The Girl on the Courthouse Steps
youtube_title: Old furnace man: you're the girl from the courthouse steps
logline: At Pell's, Nora meets Gus Moretti, who has guarded a cold furnace for twelve years. He remembers her — the girl on the courthouse steps nobody listened to.
hook: The beam drops. A stooped old man in an undershirt stands by the furnace, both hands scarred from old burns. He studies her a long time. "You're the girl who talked to the reporters on the courthouse steps."
mid_hook: She says, "I said everything Walter made has his name inside. Nobody listened." Gus doesn't answer. He turns and yanks the tarp off Furnace No. 3.
extra_hooks: "You've been here this whole time?" Gus glances at the black car outside and asks nothing. "The plant died. The furnace didn't."
conflict: She needs to know if the plant still works. The old man doesn't talk, doesn't throw her out, and won't say why he never left in twelve years.
turn: She thought nobody remembered what she said twelve years ago. The man guarding the cold furnace knew her at a glance — somebody had been listening that day.

cliffhanger.text: The tarp slides off. A dust-caked brick furnace, its mouth black as a well. Gus pats the cold brick. "Nobody's lit her in twelve years." Nora lays her palm on it. Cold as ice.
cliffhanger.question: Can Number Three ever relight?

spectacle: The tarp slides off a brick furnace two people tall; twelve years of dust falls like snow; the furnace mouth is pitch black.
glamour_shot: She presses her palm to the cold brick, hair falling beside her face, eyes closed for a beat, the thin burn scar inside her wrist against the brick.
general_payoffs: Gus recognizes her: the girl who spoke up for Walter on the courthouse steps
Furnace No. 3 is still there, cold for twelve years

title: No Hot Furnace
youtube_title: Six months, no hot furnace. So she draws and a kid blows
logline: Dr. Brandt bans hot-furnace work for six months. Nora can only draw and call the moves, so she hands the blowpipe to Gus's loud grandson.
hook: Merrow General, follow-up visit. Dr. Brandt pauses a second. "Six months. No hot furnace." Nora looks at her hands. "So ten more weeks."
mid_hook: A motorbike roars into Pell's. Buzz cut, earring, heat sleeves on both arms. "Grandpa! Who's this?" Gus: "Your teacher." Sparks: "Huh?"
extra_hooks: At the small practice furnace, Sparks blows his first cup. It slumps sideways with a soft pop. Gus: "Crooked." Sparks: "I know it's crooked!" Chalk on the wall: CROOKED — 1.
conflict: She has to make glass that proves who she is, but she can't touch hot glass for ten weeks. All she can do is draw and call the moves, with an apprentice who has never blown a straight cup as her hands.
turn: She thought no furnace meant no work. Standing behind Sparks, calling speed and breath, she finds she remembers every move. Her hands are benched. Her eyes aren't.

cliffhanger.text: Sparks panics and swings the pipe too fast. A glob of orange-hot glass slides off the tip and drops straight toward her feet—
cliffhanger.question: Will it land on her?

spectacle: The practice furnace glows orange; a glowing gather hangs from the pipe tip like a small sun in the dim plant.
glamour_shot: She stands behind the safety line, goggles pushed up on her head, apron tied tight, signalling with her hands and calling the count, furnace light in her eyes.
general_payoffs: She has an apprentice: Gus's grandson Sparks
She finds she still remembers every glassblowing move

title: Somebody Pulled Me Back
youtube_title: Hot glass fell at her feet. Someone pulled her back. Again
logline: Gus yanks Nora clear of the hot glass. She remembers someone doing that when she was nineteen but not who — and the rent figure makes Peg drop her pen.
hook: Gus jerks her back. The glass hisses onto the steel plate. For a second she sees the furnace at nineteen — a hand pulling her away. Breathless: "I remember. Somebody pulled me back." Gus says nothing.
mid_hook: Peg sits on a bench in the corner with her ledger, not looking up. "Sand's thirty-two bucks a bag. Blow carefully." The chalk on the wall now reads: CROOKED — 20.
extra_hooks: Dana calls. "The prosecutor's office took it. Reyes will review it." Nora looks at the bare wall. "Then I need a glass tube."
conflict: To work here she has to pay market rent — clause two. Sparks has ruined twenty pieces, the sand is going fast, and all she has is what's left from Peg's pawned ring.
turn: She thought rent was the smallest problem. Then Theo runs the market rate, and she can't cover a single month. The door is open. Walking through it costs money.

cliffhanger.text: Theo turns the tablet around. "Market rate. Per month." Peg glances over Nora's shoulder, sucks in a breath, and her pen hits the floor.
cliffhanger.question: Can she pay that rent?

spectacle: A glob of hot glass lands on a black steel plate, hisses out white smoke, and fades slowly from orange to dark red.
glamour_shot: Pulled behind Gus, goggles slipped to her forehead, she breathes hard and watches the glass dim, as if looking for a lost memory.
general_payoffs: She's unhurt; Gus pulled her clear in time
The prosecutor's office accepted the forgery complaint for review

title: I Pay for My Own Doors
youtube_title: Market-rate rent. She sets her old wedding ring on the table
logline: To honor clause two, Nora pays market rent. She trades the wedding ring Grant once gave her for a month of Furnace No. 3 and signs a lease with Ashford Construction.
hook: She takes Grant's old wedding ring from her wallet and sets it by the lease. "This covers a month." Peg picks up her pen and sniffs. "Told you it'd come in handy."
mid_hook: Ashford Construction boardroom. She signs as tenant. "Clause two. I pay for my own doors." Elias signs as landlord with his right hand. His left stays in his pocket.
extra_hooks: Sparks hangs off the doorframe. "So what do we call this place?" She looks at the cold furnace. "When she's lit. Then we name it."
conflict: She won't take a cent from him — even the rent is market rate. But Number Three's burner is shot, and fixing it costs money she doesn't have.
turn: She thought the repair bill was another wall. Elias slides the estimate back: the furnace is the landlord's equipment, so repairs are the landlord's job. He isn't giving her money — just a line already in the lease.

cliffhanger.text: Elias sets the burner estimate in front of her. "The furnace is mine. I fix it. The fire, you light." Pen in hand, she stares at the line marked REPAIRS.
cliffhanger.question: Does that break clause two?

spectacle: On the long boardroom table at Ashford Construction: a lease, an old wedding ring and a furnace estimate in a row; all of Port Merrow beyond the floor-to-ceiling windows.
glamour_shot: She signs the lease, the last stroke flicking outward like finishing a glass cane; hair beside her face, the first hint of certainty at her mouth.
general_payoffs: Grant's old wedding ring pays her first month; she signs a market-rate lease with Ashford Construction
Pell's is hers to rent

title: One Panel per Slot
youtube_title: Twelve empty slots on the wall. When they're full, he's done
logline: Nora builds the case tracker and a twelve-slot evidence rack on Pell's wall. But on the night of the first test fire, the twelve-year-old gas line gives out first.
hook: Dana flips to the repair clause and taps it twice. "Landlord fixes his own furnace. That's not fighting for you. Clause two holds." Nora signs the estimate.
mid_hook: She nails a long glass tube to the wall and engraves six words: REPORT, CHARGES, INVESTIGATION, ARRAIGNMENT, TRIAL, SENTENCING. A glass bead drops in — tink — and stops at REPORT.
extra_hooks: She drags an old twelve-slot sample rack out of storage and hangs it by the tube. "One panel per slot. Only what the prosecutor accepts." Sparks: "And when all twelve are full?" "Then he's sentenced."
conflict: She wants everyone to see, every day, where the case stands. But there's no evidence on the wall yet, and Number Three still isn't lit.
turn: Everyone thinks a fixed burner means fire. At the first test late at night, the twelve-year-old gas line gives out — the flame blows back out of the furnace.

cliffhanger.text: Late-night test fire. The old burner coughs black smoke — bang — and flame blows back out the mouth. Gus, in a face shield, slams the gas off. "Flashback. Line's too old." The plant fills with smoke.
cliffhanger.question: Is Number Three finished?

spectacle: A long glass tube on the red brick wall, a bead sliding — tink — to REPORT; beside it twelve empty rack slots form a blank wall under the lamp.
glamour_shot: On a ladder nailing up the tube, sleeves rolled to the elbow, goggles on her head; she turns to answer Sparks and her hair swings.
general_payoffs: The case tracker is up; the bead sits on REPORT
The twelve-slot evidence rack is hung; rule: only what the prosecutor accepts gets engraved

title: Number Three Lights
youtube_title: Twelve years cold, the furnace lights. She names the studio
logline: Gus replaces the line overnight and Furnace No. 3 lights for the first time in twelve years. Nora names the studio — and turns to find someone at the steel door.
hook: Near dawn, Gus crawls out from under the furnace, face black with soot, and gives the new fitting one last turn. "Again."
mid_hook: Whoomp. Number Three wakes. Orange fire floods out over Gus, Sparks, Peg and Nora — the first time in twelve years. Gus turns away and wipes his eyes with the back of his hand.
extra_hooks: In chalk on an old board she writes one word: REMELT. "Anything we ruin, anything that breaks — it all goes back in." Sparks yells, "Great name!" Peg: "Inside voice."
conflict: One more flashback and the old furnace may be done for good. She can't work it herself; she can only watch Gus and Sparks bring it up.
turn: Everyone thinks the fire is her win. When it catches, the one crying is Gus. To him, this was never just a furnace.

cliffhanger.text: She turns. Elias stands outside the steel door, backlit, left hand in his pocket, his face out of the fire's reach. Before she can speak, he walks off into the morning fog.
cliffhanger.question: Why did he come to watch?

spectacle: Furnace No. 3 lights for the first time in twelve years; orange light pours out and floods the red brick, the glass tube and the twelve empty slots.
glamour_shot: Firelight on the goggles pushed up on her forehead, hair lifted by the heat; she stands in the glow with color in her face for the first time.
general_payoffs: Furnace No. 3 lights for the first time in twelve years
The studio is named Remelt

title: A Light for the Ferry
youtube_title: A ferry chandelier, judged blind. No names. She's got this
logline: Theo drops off a notice for a blind competition at the ferry terminal and leaves. Nora wants an unsigned chandelier to be her first commission — but the moment she orders sand, word reaches Grant.
hook: Next morning, a notice sits under a weight on the workbench. Theo, in the doorway: "Boss said leave it here." It reads: New ferry terminal lobby chandelier. Blind competition. No names on entries.
mid_hook: Ferry terminal briefing. Project officer Fiona Marsh hugs a thick spec binder. "We judge the specs. Not the names. Entries due in ten days."
extra_hooks: She spreads out the sketch: twenty-four blue panels falling in layers like waves. Sparks: "How blue?" "The harbor. Right at dawn."
conflict: It's her first possible commission since the divorce — no name, no Mrs. Ashford. But to fire that blue she needs enough sand and batch, and she can only afford to buy once.
turn: She thought a blind competition was the cleanest fight there is — nobody knows who entered. But as she leaves the supply yard, the owner picks up his phone.

cliffhanger.text: At Doyle Sand & Batch she orders twenty bags and walks out. Hank Doyle answers his phone, low. "Mr. Whitlock? Yeah. She just ordered sand." He looks up at her back.
cliffhanger.question: What will Grant cut off?

spectacle: The new ferry terminal lobby, three stories tall and empty; light from the skylight falls on a bare hanging point at its center.
glamour_shot: She stands in the empty lobby looking up at the hanging point, shoulder-length hair, work jacket, skylight falling on her upturned face.
general_payoffs: She enters the ferry terminal blind competition: twenty-four panels of harbor-dawn blue
She spends the last of her money on twenty bags of sand

title: Cut Off
youtube_title: One night before entries close, every sand supplier says no
logline: The night before the deadline, the sand stops coming. Nora calls every supplier in town and they all say no — Whitlock Home is their biggest client.
hook: The night before the deadline, Hank's truck never shows. On the phone, he won't quite look her in the voice. "Out of stock. Try next month."
mid_hook: She calls them one by one. Every one is sold out. The last owner sighs. "Look, ma'am. Whitlock Home is our biggest client."
extra_hooks: Peg rolls up her sleeves and heads for the door. "I'll go yell at him." Nora blocks her. "No. Win the fight, still no sand."
conflict: Entries are due at nine tomorrow morning. The furnace can't go cold, and the bins are empty. She can't raid anyone's warehouse, and she can't let Elias make one call — clause two.
turn: She thought one supplier had run dry. After calling the whole city, she knows: Grant doesn't have to show up. He only has to remind everyone who their biggest client is.

cliffhanger.text: Midnight. Number Three roars; the sand bins are empty. Sparks kicks one over. "No sand. What are we melting?" The clock hits twelve. Nine hours to the deadline.
cliffhanger.question: Where will she find sand?

spectacle: Remelt at midnight: Number Three's fire reflected in a row of empty sand bins; the old wall clock's hands meet at twelve.
glamour_shot: She sits on the floor by the empty bins, back to the red brick, firelight jumping on her profile, phone still in hand, eyes dry.
general_payoffs: She stops Peg — no yelling, no grabbing, only the front door

title: Then We Mix Our Own
youtube_title: No sand anywhere. Then: I still remember the Pell recipe
logline: No sand the night before the deadline. Gus drags out Pell's batch, untouched for twelve years. Nora can't work the furnace, so she uses her hands, the scale and her eyes to mix that blue.
hook: Deep in the storeroom, Gus drags out a row of sacks nobody has opened in twelve years, stamped with a faded PELL. "I still remember the Pell recipe."
mid_hook: She rolls up her sleeves. "Then we mix our own." Banned from the hot furnace, she kneels at the scale, spoon by spoon. Gus calls a line; she corrects it. "Cobalt. Two grams less."
extra_hooks: Four a.m. Peg is asleep on the long bench, hugging her ledger. Sparks lays his jacket over her and tiptoes back to the furnace.
conflict: Nine hours to make a new batch from twelve-year-old materials. She can only work the scale and call the moves; Gus is old, Sparks still blows crooked, and one wrong spoonful means starting over.
turn: Grant thought cutting off the sand would cut her off. But Pell's storeroom still holds twelve-year-old batch, and Gus still holds Walter's recipe. Grant can shut down suppliers. He can't shut down Pell's.

cliffhanger.text: Dawn. Gus opens the annealer; Sparks lifts out the first sheet with long tongs. Morning light passes through it, and the whole brick wall turns harbor-dawn blue. Nora, softly: "Glass cools slowly. So do people." Her mother's words.
cliffhanger.question: Will this blue win the ferry?

spectacle: Morning light through a fresh sheet of blue glass turns the whole red brick wall harbor-dawn blue; the tracker tube and the twelve slots glow blue too.
glamour_shot: She kneels at the scale, spoon by spoon, sleeves rolled up, white powder on the thin burn scar inside her wrist, furnace light on her focused profile.
general_payoffs: Pell's twelve-year-old batch makes the blue she wanted
The first sheet comes out before the deadline
Gus says it out loud for the first time: he remembers Walter's recipes
